titulo_es: Fronting: moving information to the beginning
descripcion_es: Placing a complement, object or predicate at the start of the sentence for emphasis, contrast or cohesion.
resumen: The normal order in English is subject + verb + complements. Moving an element to the beginning (fronting) highlights it or links it to what came before. Sometimes it causes inversion of the subject and the verb.

filas: That kind of behaviour I simply cannot accept.
In the corner stood an old piano.
Here comes the bus. / Off they went.
Tired as she was, she kept working.
More important is the question of cost.
Link with what came before (with inversion)
So strong was the wind that trees fell.
Such was the demand that tickets sold out.

items: With a fronted object there is NO inversion: This book I really enjoyed.

With a place adverbial followed by a verb of position or movement (stand, lie, sit, come, go), the whole verb is inverted: Down the hill rolled the ball. But not if the subject is a pronoun: Down the hill it rolled.
Adjective/adverb + as/though + subject + verb expresses concession: Much as I like him, I can't agree.
Patterns with inversion and an auxiliary: So + adj. + auxiliary/be + subject + that…

explicacion.texto: Fronting is very useful for cohesion: start the sentence with known information and leave the new information for the end. Also relevant is…, Equally worrying is…, Of particular concern is… are valuable formulas in an oral presentation.

ejemplos.frase: Of particular concern is the rise in youth unemployment.
ejemplos.traduccion: Especialmente preocupante es el aumento del paro juvenil.

ejemplos.frase: On the table lay a letter addressed to me.
ejemplos.traduccion: Sobre la mesa había una carta dirigida a mí.

ejemplos.frase: Strange as it may seem, I've never been to the beach.
ejemplos.traduccion: Por extraño que parezca, nunca he ido a la playa.

ejemplos.frase: So loud was the music that we couldn't hear each other.
ejemplos.traduccion: La música estaba tan alta que no nos oíamos.

ejemplos.frase: Such was her talent that she won every competition.
ejemplos.traduccion: Era tal su talento que ganaba todos los concursos.

ejemplos.frase: His first novel I loved; his second I found disappointing.
ejemplos.traduccion: Su primera novela me encantó; la segunda me decepcionó.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Such the demand was that prices doubled.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Such was the demand that prices doubled.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: With fronted such, be comes immediately after it: Such was + subject.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: So tired I was that I fell asleep.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: So tired was I that I fell asleep.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After fronted so + adjective, the verb goes before the subject.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Although tired as he was, he finished the race.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Tired as he was, he finished the race.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: The construction with as is already concessive; although is not added.
With a pronoun subject there is no inversion after a place adverbial.

ejercicios.frase: So unexpected ___ that nobody knew how to react.
ejercicios.explicacion: The pattern So + adjective + auxiliary/be + subject + that… from Rules and keys applies: when so + adjective comes first, be goes before the subject. The clue is So unexpected at the start and the later that introducing the consequence. There is also an agreement trap: news is uncountable and singular, so the verb is was. The correct answer is was the news: inversion and singular at the same time.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Fronted so + adjective requires inversion; news is singular.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tan inesperada fue la noticia que nadie supo cómo reaccionar.

por_opcion.the news was: Incorrect: after fronted so + adjective you need inversion; subject–verb order does not work here.
por_opcion.was the news: Correct: there is inversion (verb before subject) and the verb is singular because news is uncountable.
por_opcion.the news were: Incorrect for two reasons: the inversion is missing and news does not take a plural verb.
por_opcion.were the news: Incorrect: the inversion is right, but news is singular and requires was.

ejercicios.frase: At the top of the hill ___ an old castle.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in Rules and keys about a place adverbial followed by a verb of position or movement (stand, lie, sit, come, go) applies: the whole verb is inverted and the noun subject goes at the end. The clue is the adverbial At the top of the hill at the start and the subject an old castle, which is a noun and not a pronoun. That is why the form is stands, with no auxiliary: the lexical verb moves in front of the subject.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Place adverbial + verb of position + noun subject.
ejercicios.traduccion: En lo alto de la colina se alza un viejo castillo.

por_opcion.it stands: Incorrect: it adds an unnecessary subject it, because the real subject is an old castle.
por_opcion.stands: Correct: after the place adverbial comes the verb of position and then the noun subject: stands an old castle.
por_opcion.standing: Incorrect: the -ing form is not a finite verb and the sentence would be left without a main verb.
por_opcion.does stand: Incorrect: this type of inversion does not use do; the whole lexical verb is fronted.

ejercicios.frase: Much ___ I admire her work, I can't support this project.
ejercicios.explicacion: The pattern adjective/adverb + as/though + subject + verb from Rules and keys applies, which expresses concession. The clue is Much at the start, followed by a clause (I admire her work) and then by a contrasting main clause. Much as means “although” or “however much” and is a fixed formula; the word that completes it is as.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por mucho que admire su trabajo, no puedo apoyar este proyecto.

por_opcion.as: Correct: much as + clause is the card's concessive formula (“however much”).
por_opcion.so: Incorrect: “much so” does not introduce a concession and the sentence would make no sense.
por_opcion.that: Incorrect: “much that” is not a concessive formula in English.
por_opcion.like: Incorrect: like does not form this structure; it is a calque of Spanish “por mucho que me guste”.

ejercicios.frase: Equally important ___ the need for training.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table pattern of a fronted adjective with inversion applies (More important is the question of cost), together with the point that fronting serves to link with what came before. The clue is Equally important at the start: after it comes be and then the subject. The real subject is the need for training, singular (need), although training is singular too; that is why the verb is is. It is a very useful presentation formula for adding an argument.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Fronted adjective + be + subject; the subject (the need) is singular.
ejercicios.traduccion: Igual de importante es la necesidad de formación.

por_opcion.are: Incorrect: the postponed subject is the need, singular, so the verb cannot be plural.
por_opcion.is: Correct: fronted adjective + be + singular subject (the need for training).
por_opcion.it is: Incorrect: it introduces an unnecessary subject it; the subject is already the need for training.
por_opcion.being: Incorrect: the -ing form leaves the sentence without a finite verb.

ejercicios.frase: ___ was the demand that the shop ran out of stock in an hour.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table pattern Such + be applies: Such was + noun + that… expresses a degree so high that it produces a consequence (“so great was… that…”). The clue is the verb was right after the gap, followed by the demand and by that. The missing word is Such, which here works as a fronted predicate; you cannot use so, which needs an adjective after it.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Such was + noun + that: so great was… that.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tal era la demanda que la tienda se quedó sin existencias en una hora.

errores_previstos.respuesta: So
errores_previstos.explicacion: So is placed before an adjective (So great was the demand…); before was + noun you need Such.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Tal
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the Spanish word; in English it is Such.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Much
errores_previstos.explicacion: Much does not form this consequence structure; the formula is Such was… that.

ejercicios.frase: Hard ___ they tried, they couldn't open the door.
ejercicios.explicacion: The pattern adjective/adverb + as/though + subject + verb from Rules and keys applies, which expresses concession. The clue is the adverb Hard at the start, followed by they tried and by a main clause with the opposite result. Both as and though are accepted, because both form this concessive structure; as is the more frequent. Although is not added in front, because the structure itself is already concessive.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Adverb + as/though + subject + verb = however much.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por mucho que lo intentaron, no pudieron abrir la puerta.

errores_previstos.respuesta: although
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although does not combine with the fronted adverb; the structure is Hard as/though they tried.

errores_previstos.respuesta: so
errores_previstos.explicacion: So would have a different meaning and require inversion; for concession you use as or though.

errores_previstos.respuesta: like
errores_previstos.explicacion: Like does not form this concessive construction.

ejercicios.frase: Of greater concern ___ the long-term effects on health.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table pattern of a fronted comparative adjective with inversion applies, together with the formula Of particular concern is… from the card's text. The clue is Of greater concern at the start: after it comes be and then the postponed subject. That subject is the long-term effects, plural, so the verb must be are. It is easy to go wrong because the verb appears before you see the subject: you have to look ahead to make it agree.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The postponed subject (the long-term effects) is plural.
ejercicios.traduccion: Más preocupantes son los efectos a largo plazo sobre la salud.

errores_previstos.respuesta: is
errores_previstos.explicacion: It agrees with concern, but the real subject is the long-term effects, plural: are.

errores_previstos.respuesta: it is
errores_previstos.explicacion: It adds an unnecessary subject; the subject is already the long-term effects.

errores_previstos.respuesta: were
errores_previstos.explicacion: It agrees in the plural, but changes the tense for no reason: the sentence is in the present.

ejercicios.frase: The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
respuestas: So boring was the film that I fell asleep.
ejercicios.explicacion: The pattern So + adjective + be + subject + that… from Rules and keys applies, with inversion. The clue is the instruction to start with So and the original sentence with so boring that. Front So boring, invert was and the film, and keep that I fell asleep: So boring was the film that I fell asleep. Without inversion the sentence would be incorrect, as the card notes among its typical mistakes.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tan aburrida era la película que me quedé dormido.

errores_previstos.respuesta: So boring the film was that I fell asleep.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The inversion is missing: after initial so + adjective, the verb goes before the subject.

errores_previstos.respuesta: So the film was boring that I fell asleep.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It separates so from the adjective; you must front the block So boring and invert was the film.

errores_previstos.respuesta: So boring was the film, I fell asleep.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It drops that; in this pattern the consequence is introduced by that.

ejercicios.frase: Although it may sound strange, I enjoy rainy days.
respuestas: Strange as it may sound, I enjoy rainy days.
Strange though it may sound, I enjoy rainy days.
ejercicios.explicacion: The pattern adjective + as/though + subject + verb for concession from Rules and keys applies. The clue is the original sentence with although and the instruction to start with Strange: the adjective moves to the start, followed by as (or though) and then the rest of the subordinate clause, it may sound. Both as and though are accepted because both form the structure. Although disappears, because the new structure is already concessive in itself.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Adjective + as/though + subject + verb for concession.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque pueda parecer extraño, disfruto de los días de lluvia.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Strange although it may sound, I enjoy rainy days.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Although does not form this pattern; after the fronted adjective comes as or though.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Strange as may it sound, I enjoy rainy days.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It inverts for no reason; in concession with as the order is subject + verb: as it may sound.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Although strange as it may sound, I enjoy rainy days.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It doubles the concession, a mistake the card lists: the structure with as already means “although”.

ejercicios.frase: The storm was so violent that the port was closed.
respuestas: Such was the violence of the storm that the port was closed.
Such was the storm's violence that the port was closed.
Such was the storm that the port was closed.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table pattern Such + be applies: Such was + noun + that… The clue is the instruction to start with Such and the original sentence with so violent that. Since such needs a noun and not an adjective, the natural thing is to nominalise: the violence of the storm (or the storm's violence). Such was the storm is also accepted, which highlights the storm itself. In every case be comes immediately after Such.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Such was + noun (the violence of…) + that.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tal fue la violencia de la tormenta que se cerró el puerto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Such violent was the storm that the port was closed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Such does not go with an adjective alone; with an adjective you use So violent was…, and with Such you need a noun.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Such the violence of the storm was that the port was closed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the mistake the card lists: with fronted such, be comes immediately after it (Such was…).

errores_previstos.respuesta: Such a violent storm was that the port was closed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It mixes two structures and leaves the sentence without a clear subject; the pattern is Such was + noun + that.

ejercicios.frase: So difficult the exam was that half the class failed.
respuestas: So difficult was the exam that half the class failed.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in Rules and keys applies: after initial so + adjective, be and the subject are inverted. The clue is So difficult at the start and the that of consequence. The given sentence keeps the normal order (the exam was), which is exactly the mistake the card points out. The correction is So difficult was the exam that half the class failed.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After initial so + adjective, be and the subject are inverted.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tan difícil fue el examen que suspendió la mitad de la clase.

errores_previstos.respuesta: So difficult the exam was that half the class failed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: was and the exam need to be inverted.

errores_previstos.respuesta: So difficult did the exam be that half the class failed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Do is not used with be; the verb itself is inverted: was the exam.

errores_previstos.respuesta: So difficult was the exam, half the class failed.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It removes that; in this pattern the consequence is introduced by that.

ejercicios.frase: Out of the cave ran they.
respuestas: Out of the cave they ran.
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in Rules and keys applies: after a place adverbial, the verb is inverted only if the subject is a noun; if it is a pronoun, there is no inversion (Down the hill it rolled). The clue is the subject they, a pronoun. That is why the correct version is Out of the cave they ran, with subject + verb order after the fronted adverbial.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With a pronoun subject there is no inversion after the place adverbial.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Out of the cave ran they.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It leaves the sentence uncorrected: with a pronoun subject there is no inversion.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Out of the cave did they run.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It brings in do as in negative inversion; this pattern uses no auxiliary and does not invert with a pronoun.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Out of the cave ran them.
errores_previstos.explicacion: As well as inverting, it uses the object pronoun them as the subject.

respuestas: Into the room walked a tall stranger
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule of a place or direction adverbial followed by a verb of movement applies: the whole verb is inverted and the noun subject goes at the end. The clue is the preposition Into, which marks direction, the verb walked and the subject a tall stranger, which is a noun. The result, Into the room walked a tall stranger, is typical of narration: it sets a scene and leaves the new information (the stranger) for the end.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Direction adverbial + verb of movement + noun subject.
ejercicios.traduccion: En la habitación entró un desconocido alto.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Into the room walked a stranger tall
errores_previstos.explicacion: It copies the Spanish order “un desconocido alto”: in English the adjective goes before the noun, a tall stranger.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Into the room did walk a tall stranger
errores_previstos.explicacion: It brings in do as in inversion after negative adverbials; after a place adverbial the lexical verb is fronted, with no auxiliary.

respuestas: Young as he is he is very wise
ejercicios.explicacion: The pattern adjective + as + subject + verb from Rules and keys applies, which expresses concession (“although he is young”). The clue is the words Young and as, which form the concessive opening, and the repetition of he is: the first belongs to the concession and the second to the main clause. The correct order is Young as he is, followed by he is very wise. In writing you would put a comma after the concession.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Adjective + as + subject + verb = although he is young.
ejercicios.traduccion: Aunque es joven, es muy sabio.

errores_previstos.respuesta: He is young as he is very wise
errores_previstos.explicacion: It keeps the Spanish order and loses the concessive structure.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Young as is he he is very wise
errores_previstos.explicacion: It inverts for no reason; in concession with as the order is subject + verb.

descripcion_larga_es: Fronting consists of taking an element out of its usual place and putting it at the start of the sentence to highlight it or link it to what came before. English has a very rigid word order, so this device is very noticeable and sometimes forces the subject and verb to be inverted. Spanish speakers find it hard because in Spanish we move words around freely, without equivalent inversion rules.

contexto.que_es: It is the fronting of an element that would normally go after the verb: an object, a place adverbial, an adjective or a structure with so or such. Depending on the pattern, the rest of the sentence keeps the normal order or inverts the verb and the subject.
contexto.por_que_importa: It serves cohesion and emphasis: you start with known information and leave the new information for the end, or you highlight the degree of something. Formulas such as Equally important is…, Of particular concern is… or Such was… are very valuable in an oral presentation or a formal essay. Using them wrongly (without inversion when it is needed, or with inversion when it is not) sounds clearly foreign.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It appears in argumentative texts, narratives and speeches: to link ideas (More important is…), describe a scene (In the corner stood…), stress a degree (So difficult was…) or concede (Strange as it may sound…). Spanish speakers tend to move the element without inverting, because in Spanish “Tan difícil fue el examen” and “Tan difícil el examen fue” sound almost equally possible, or else they also invert with pronouns, where English does not.
